title: Phrase-Matrix Suite (pre-registration)
description:
A PRE-REGISTERED experiment: the fixtures, the phrases and the arm plan, all written down BEFORE any live inference.

The point of pre-registration is narrow and load-bearing. An open-vocabulary organ can be made to look good by trying phrases until one lands, and the resulting number is not a hit-rate — it is the outcome of a search, reported as if it were a measurement. So the phrase list is frozen and hashed here, and `lock` records the digest. Once collection starts the runner recomputes that digest and refuses to proceed if it moved.

This file therefore has one job the schema cannot enforce and a human must: it has to be written before anyone knows what the answers are.

pre_registered_at.description: When the phrases were frozen. Prose, for the reader; the digest in `lock` is what the runner enforces.

actuator_lock.description: Inherited from HARNESS-001C unchanged: exactly one actuator, for every capture in the suite.

call_budget.description: Per capture. A matrix of N captures is N budgets of one, never one budget of N — a shared pool is a pool something can borrow against.

phrases_sha256.description: Digest over the frozen phrase families. Recomputed at every `--live` and every `--report`; a mismatch after collection has begun is fatal, because a phrase list edited mid-collection turns measurement into result-searching and leaves no trace otherwise.

fixtures_sha256.description: Digest over the fixture ids and their content hashes. Swapping an image under a stable id would silently change what every phrase was tested against.

source.description: Where the claim comes from — a repo path, not a recollection.

documented_subject.description: What the REPOSITORY says this shows. Null when the repo says nothing; an identification made by looking at it is not documentation and belongs in `observed`.

documented_tradition.description: Culture/period ONLY where the repo sources it. Null is the honest and common value: recognising a sculpture is not the same as the repository documenting it.

known_confounds.description: Image conditions the repo already records as affecting results — e.g. a blended grain/texture layer. Declared HERE, before collection, so a fixture cannot be blamed for a result after the fact.

observed.description: What is visible, marked as observation rather than documentation.

role.description: `control_condition` marks a fixture included to vary ONE declared image condition against the primary.

phrase_families.description: FROZEN before the first live call. Members may not be added afterwards for any reason, and least of all in response to a failure.

role.description: `availability_control` is the gate: if it returns nothing on a fixture, NO phrase failure on that fixture may be attributed to the phrase, because the instrument was not shown to be working there.

expectation.description: What the family is for. Never a prediction the scoring may consult — recorded so a reader can see what was expected before the numbers arrived.

justification.description: Required for anything added to the card's own list. Only legal BEFORE the first live call.

wrapper_equivalence.description: The representative subset run through the PRODUCTION actuator on every image, so wrapper equivalence is tested beyond the original fixture.

samples.description: At least five independent receipts. One repeat that happened to agree is not stability.

planning_only.description: Declared IN ADVANCE, as the directive requires: planner samples never grant SAM attempts. A planning-only receipt is not an organ result and the scoring may not read it as one.

model_contract.description: Model, version and sampling settings under which the samples are comparable. Receipts from different contracts are not evidence about the same thing.

expected_invariants.description: Structural claims the suite asserts about EVERY capture. Machine-checkable, and checked.
